newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: IMF says Portugal must cut spending for EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Portugal must cut spending for EMU - paper.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) believes that Portugal can meet the EMU budget deficit target of three percent next year but only if it takes tough action on public spending, according to a report in the Diario Economico.

Citing what it said was a confidential report, the newspaper said that the Fund saw the need for a freeze on public sector wages, a reduction in the number of civil servants and cuts in current spending by ministries.
"Our projections indicate that the mere freezing in nominal terms...will not be enough," the Fund was quoted as saying.

Portugal's Socialist government, which is forecasting the deficit will fall to around four percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year from some five percent in 1995, argues that the jump to the EMU target can be achieved without huge sacrifices.

Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco was quoted by Portuguese news agency Lusa as saying in Washington, where he is attending the Fund's annual meeting, that the IMF was entitled to make its forecasts just like "any academic on the basis of a model."
But it was the government that took the political and economic decisions, he added.

Diario Economico said that in the report, drawn up after a visit to Portugal in July, the IMF said that the alternative to real cuts in spending was higher taxes, something that the government has consistently rejected.
It recommended a rise in Value Added Tax (VAT) as the levels currently applied in Portugal were below European averages.
